audit.why: Full phases[0..6].side and content win[0..6] both read Zed on every row, matching the packet levelChart and the FAVOURED 4/10 rating. Nothing to move.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text described the stage gates without a single cooldown, so "commit when his stun is down" had no length attached to it.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11 at 1050 range — the longest-feeling window in the lane and the one that decides every commit. Eye of Destruction is 14/13/12/11/10 at 1000 and is what sets the orb up.
audit.corrected: 13s written into the level 3, 4-5 and level 6 stages so each spike is keyed to a real number.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never said what Rite of the Arcane does to Xerath himself. It was described only as a zoning tool 'to zone you'.
audit.why: Riot text: "Xerath immobilizes himself and gains numerous long-range barrages." A channelling Xerath cannot walk, which is exactly the state Death Mark wants him in — and it is also why lingering after your R gets you barraged from 5000 range.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[1].text, breakdown.carry and dontsFull[2].d.

edits.after: Xerath wins by chaining Eye of Destruction's slow into Shocking Orb and finishing you from a range you never closed.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Living Shadow (swap) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb (E): 13s at rank 1, 1050 range, and his only CC — dodge it and the artillery never converts into a kill. - Eye of Destruction is 14s and its slow is what sets the orb up, so never walk a straight line after it lands. - Living Shadow's 20s answers a missed dodge, never a poke.

edits.before: Xerath is a immobile artillery mage whose whole game is landing skillshots at max range; sidestep his Q (Arcanopulse) and W (Eye of Destruction), then W-swap the gap and punish him the moment his stun (E, Shocking Orb) is down.
edits.after: Xerath is an immobile artillery mage whose whole game is landing skillshots at range; sidestep his Q (Arcanopulse) and W (Eye of Destruction), then W-swap the gap and punish the moment Shocking Orb's 13 seconds at rank 1 start ticking.

edits.before: Death Mark ignores his poke-and-pray gameplan: all-in when his E stun is on cooldown, W onto him, and R deletes him before he can channel R (Rite of the Arcane) to zone you.
edits.after: Death Mark ignores his poke-and-pray gameplan: all-in while Shocking Orb is on its 13s, W onto him, and remember Rite of the Arcane immobilises Xerath himself — a channelling Xerath cannot walk away.

notes: Chart was already consistent across both layers and the packet (Zed on all seven rows), so no side or win[N] edits. Added the interaction the page never stated: Rite of the Arcane immobilises Xerath for its duration, which is both the best moment to mark him and the reason lingering after your own R gets you barraged from 5000 range. Left alone deliberately: the kit lists Arcanopulse at 750 range, which is shorter than Zed's 900 Q and does not match how the ability plays when charged, so no claim about out-ranging him was written anywhere.
